1.1:
Approach Trace every stage a deal passes through from a sales opportunity to recognized revenue, and map each stage to the standard and custom objects in the CPQ & Revenue Cloud Academy data model. The point is to see the "round trip" — a contract becomes a renewal opportunity, a quote becomes an order, an order generates billing schedules, and revenue recognition closes the loop.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Opportunity — the sell starts with an Opportunity. Capture ARR__c, expected revenue and Renewal_Date__c (for renewals).
  2. Quote — CPQ builds a Quote with QuoteLineItems, Total_ARR__c and Discount_Percent__c; configure before pricing.
  3. Approval — pass the quote through ApprovalRoutingService; log the outcome on Approval_Log__c (Approval_Type__c, Decision__c, Discount_Percent__c).
  4. Contract — ContractGenerationService turns the accepted quote into a Contract with CPQ_Contract_Status__c, ARR__c, Auto_Renew__c and term fields.
  5. Order — OrderFulfillmentService creates the Order; track Fulfillment_Status__c and ERP_Order_Number__c.
  6. Billing — BillingScheduleService produces Revenue_Schedule__c periods with Recognition_Method__c, Amount__c and Recognition_Date__c.
  7. Recognition — RevenueRecognitionService moves amounts to Recognized_Amount__c and flips Status__c.
  8. Renewal loop — RenewalQuoteService creates Renewal_Opportunity__c records; the cycle repeats.
text
Opportunity -> Quote -> Approval(Approval_Log__c) -> Contract
   -> Order -> Revenue_Schedule__c (billing/recognition)
   -> Renewal_Opportunity__c -> new Quote  (loop)

Expected result — a lifecycle map where each stage owns one or two objects, e.g. stage "Bill & Recognize" owns Revenue_Schedule__c, and the "Renew" stage owns Renewal_Opportunity__c. A quiz answer that names all eight stages in order scores a full mark.

Common mistakes

  • Skipping the renewal/amendment loop and drawing a straight line from contract to cash.
  • Confusing Order (fulfillment) with Revenue_Schedule__c (billing).
  • Placing approval after contracting instead of before quote acceptance.
  • Treating Opportunity and Quote as the same object — the quote is the configurable, pricable artifact.
1.2:
Approach Decide between legacy CPQ (managed package, SBQQ__ objects) and Revenue Lifecycle Management (RLM, next-gen on core objects like ProductCatalog and PriceBookEntry) by judging the scenario's requirements: catalog complexity, subscription vs one-time, cloud-native vs existing org, and migration appetite. Use the two engines from the fundamentals module as a decision matrix.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Read the scenario and list hard requirements (subscriptions, amendments, native core objects, API version 68.0).
  2. If the org already runs legacy CPQ with SBQQ__ data and needs continuity, choose CPQ.
  3. If the deal is pure subscription/recurring revenue with assets and price books, let RLM drive from core Product2/PriceBookEntry/ProductCatalog.
  4. If the scenario mixes one-time equipment and subscriptions, prefer CPQ for legacy reasons or plan a migration project.
  5. Justify the answer with one line per requirement mapped to an engine.

10.1:
Approach One order becomes the series of Revenue_Schedule__c periods the customer is invoiced on. The schedule is straight-line: an equal Amount__c per period, with any rounding remainder placed on the last period so the rows sum exactly to the order value.

  1. Select Recognition_Method__c = 'Straight Line' for the schedule.
  2. Call BillingScheduleService.buildBillingSchedule(order.Id) to generate one row per month.
  3. Verify each row carries Period__c (M1…M12), a monthly Recognition_Date__c, Status__c = 'Pending' and Amount__c.
  4. Confirm SUM(Amount__c) equals Order.Total_ARR__c.
apex
Revenue_Schedule__c[] schedule =
    BillingScheduleService.buildBillingSchedule(order.Id);

System.assertEquals(12, schedule.size());

Decimal total = 0;
for (Revenue_Schedule__c row : schedule) {
    total += row.Amount__c;
}
System.assertEquals(order.Total_ARR__c.setScale(2), total.setScale(2));
System.assertEquals('Straight Line', schedule[0].Recognition_Method__c);

Expected result Twelve monthly rows for a twelve-month term, period labels sequential, Recognition_Method__c = 'Straight Line', and SUM(Amount__c) equal to the order ARR to the cent — the remainder sitting on period 12, never lost.

Common mistakes

  • Dividing evenly (1200 / 12 = 100) and silently dropping the remainder when the annual value doesn't split exactly — rows then never reconcile to ARR.
  • Putting the rounding delta on the first period, distorting the opening month.
  • Generating a fixed 12 rows even when Contract_Term_Months__c is 24 or 36 — the count must follow the term.
  • Forgetting Recognition_Method__c, so recognition logic later has no method to honor.
  • Leaving Status__c off the rows; recognition depends on it.
10.2:
Approach Recognition is date-driven and deterministic: a row is recognized only when its Recognition_Date__c is on or before today; rows dated in the future stay Pending. Re-running the job must change nothing.

  1. Load the order's schedule lines.
  2. Call RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue(order.Id) to evaluate the batch.
  3. For each row with Recognition_Date__c <= today, set Status__c = 'Recognized' and Recognized_Amount__c = Amount__c.
  4. Leave future-dated rows untouched and re-verify the recognized total matches the elapsed periods.
apex
RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue(order.Id);

for (Revenue_Schedule__c line : BillingScheduleService.buildBillingSchedule(order.Id)) {
    if (line.Recognition_Date__c <= Date.today()) {
        line.Status__c = 'Recognized';
        line.Recognized_Amount__c = line.Amount__c;
    }
}

Expected result All past-due periods are Recognized with Recognized_Amount__c populated; future periods remain Pending. The cumulative recognized total equals the periods elapsed, and a second identical run changes no rows (idempotent).

Common mistakes

  • Recognizing the entire schedule in one shot regardless of Recognition_Date__c — the accounting dies.
  • Comparing with < instead of <=, so today's period is always one day late.
  • Updating Status__c but never Recognized_Amount__c, starving rollupAccountARR of value.
  • Double-counting on re-runs because already-recognized rows were not excluded (Status__c != 'Recognized' guard).
  • Deriving dates from order creation rather than the schedule's own Recognition_Date__c.

11.2:
Approach In RLM a subscription is modeled as a sellable product, a price, a term, and a recurring asset — not a one-time transaction. Recognize the subscription over its term and predict its renewal from the same contract.

  1. Add the subscription to the sellable catalog: a Product2 inside ProductCatalog with ProductSellingModel describing how it sells (e.g. Subscription).
  2. Give it a sellable price with a PriceBookEntry (product + currency) so it can be quoted.
  3. Quote and sell it: QuoteLineItem carries List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, Discount_Percent__c and ARR__c; Quote.Contract_Term_Months__c pins the term.
  4. Generate the contract and order, then let BillingScheduleService turn the order into monthly Revenue_Schedule__c rows (Straight Line over the term).
  5. Recognize over time with RevenueRecognitionService and pre-build the renewal with RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline, applying Uplift_Percent__c.
soql
SELECT Id, AccountId, StartDate, EndDate, ContractTerm, Status,
       ARR__c, Auto_Renew__c, Renewal_Term_Months__c, Uplift_Percent__c
FROM Contract
WHERE ARR__c > 0
ORDER BY EndDate, Id

Expected result One quoted subscription produces one PriceBookEntry-priced quote, one contract, one order, N monthly Revenue_Schedule__c rows that sum to ARR, progressive recognized amounts, and a Renewal_Opportunity__c whose ARR__c already includes uplift before the term ends.

Common mistakes

  • Modeling the subscription as a one-off product with Immediate recognition — the revenue curve is wrong for SaaS.
  • Quoting without a PriceBookEntry, so the product has no currency price.
  • Ignoring Contract_Term_Months__c and defaulting every subscription to 12 months.
  • Forgetting co-termination when a subscription is added mid-term — the new asset must slide to the anchor end date.
  • Referencing SBQQ__Subscription__c in RLM instead of the native asset + schedule model.
12.1:
Approach Platform events decouple producers from consumers. Revenue_Sync__e carries Source_Object__c, Payload__c, Direction__c, Status__c, Correlation_Id__c, Integration_Type__c, Retry_Count__c and Endpoint__c. Producers publish with EventBus.publish; subscribers consume via a trigger on the event object.

  1. Build the Revenue_Sync__e payload: serialize the quote/order state into Payload__c, set Direction__c = 'Outbound', Integration_Type__c, Endpoint__c and a unique Correlation_Id__c.
  2. Publish in a batch (EventBus.publish(events)) — never per-record inside a loop.
  3. Subscribe with an after insert trigger on Revenue_Sync__e that reads Trigger.new and guards re-entry via QuoteTriggerHandlerService.shouldRun.
  4. Make the consumer idempotent: keyed on Correlation_Id__c so a replay does not double-apply.
apex
List<Revenue_Sync__e> events = new List<Revenue_Sync__e>();
for (Id quoteId : quoteIds) {
    events.add(new Revenue_Sync__e(
        Source_Object__c = 'Quote',
        Payload__c = JSON.serialize(aPayloadMap),
        Direction__c = 'Outbound',
        Status__c = 'Published',
        Correlation_Id__c = String.valueOf(Crypto.getRandomLong()),
        Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync',
        Endpoint__c = 'RevenueCloudEventBus'
    ));
}
EventBus.publish(events);

Expected result Every approval-state change emits exactly one Revenue_Sync__e; the subscriber consumes it, logs the source/status/direction, and re-processing the same Correlation_Id__c applies no duplicate side effect.

Common mistakes

  • Publishing inside a loop — batch EventBus.publish once for the whole list.
  • Omitting Correlation_Id__c, killing dedupe and replay safety.
  • Subscribing with side effects that aren't idempotent (same event consumed twice = double ARR/order).
  • Forgetting the recursion guard; a subscriber that writes to the source object re-fires the trigger.
  • Ignoring Retry_Count__c/Status__c, so failed deliveries are silently lost instead of queued for replay.
12.2:
Approach An external pricing service returns the authoritative net price; CRM stores the result on the line while the platform keeps the audit. Because callouts inside triggers are synchronous, route them through a Queueable/@future and keep the flow async.

  1. Resolve the endpoint from Revenue_Sync__e.Endpoint__c or a Named Credential (never a hard-coded URL).
  2. Issue an HttpRequest (GET/POST) carrying the product family and List_Unit_Price__c; set a timeout.
  3. JSON.deserialize the response into a price map keyed by line/pricebook entry.
  4. Write Net_Unit_Price__c (and recompute Discount_Percent__c), then call QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals so Total_ARR__c stays honest.
  5. On failure, publish a Revenue_Sync__e with Status__c = 'Integration Failed' and increment Retry_Count__c for replay.
apex
public class PricingSyncService implements Queueable {
    public void execute(QueueableContext context) {
        for (QuoteLineItem line : [SELECT Id, List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c
                                   FROM QuoteLineItem WHERE Id IN :lineIds]) {
            HttpRequest req = new HttpRequest();
            req.setEndpoint('callout:PricingAPI/price');
            req.setMethod('POST');
            req.setBody(JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                'family' => line.PricebookEntryId,
                'listPrice' => line.List_Unit_Price__c
            }));
            HttpResponse res = new Http().send(req);
            PriceResult p = (PriceResult) JSON.deserialize(res.getBody(), PriceResult.class);
            line.Net_Unit_Price__c = p.netPrice;
        }
        update lines;
        QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals(quoteIds);
    }
}

Expected result Quoted lines carry Net_Unit_Price__c and Discount_Percent__c from the API, Total_ARR__c reflects the new nets, and any failed callout is recorded with Retry_Count__c and a replayable audit event.

Common mistakes

  • Doing the callout synchronously in a trigger — fails against the "no callouts in triggers" limit.
  • Hard-coding the URL instead of the Named Credential/Endpoint__c; environment drift breaks config.
  • Skipping the timeout — a hung pricing API burns transaction limits.
  • Not cascading the price change into recalculateTotals, so the quote total drifts from the lines.
  • Hiding failures — a silent 500 leaves Retry_Count__c at 0 and the deal un-priced.
13.1:
Approach The pipeline is the sum of ARR not yet booked: quotes awaiting approval, open renewal opportunities, and recognized revenue to date. One consolidated view must reconcile against Account.Current_ARR__c.

  1. Define the stages — Pending approval, Open renewal, Recognized.
  2. Report quotes grouped by Status then Approval_Status__c, summing Quote.Total_ARR__c (the repo's Quote_Pipeline_ARR report does exactly this).
  3. Aggregate renewals from Renewal_Opportunity__c.ARR__c where Status__c = 'Open'.
  4. Fold recognized amounts in via the Revenue_Schedule__c rollup to compare against Account.Current_ARR__c.
soql
SELECT StageName, COUNT(Id) Deals, SUM(ARR__c) PipelineARR
FROM Opportunity
WHERE IsWon = false AND ARR__c != null
GROUP BY StageName ORDER BY SUM(ARR__c) DESC

SELECT Account__c, SUM(Recognized_Amount__c) RecognizedTotal
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
WHERE Status__c = 'Recognized'
GROUP BY Account__c
ORDER BY SUM(Recognized_Amount__c) DESC

Expected result One report shows pipeline ARR by stage; the sum of quote pipeline ARR plus open renewal ARR reconciles to the account's target, and recognized totals match Account.Current_ARR__c.

Common mistakes

  • Mixing total contract value with annual ARR — pipeline statements must be in one unit.
  • Counting the same deal twice (in Opportunity.ARR__c and Quote.Total_ARR__c).
  • Ignoring Approval_Status__c, so unapproved quotes inflate the pipeline.
  • Querying schedules without the Status__c = 'Recognized' filter and overstating ARR.
  • Omitting a date filter on Recognition_Date__c when building trend comparisons.
13.2:
Approach Discount leakage is the money given away between list and net. At the opportunity level it is Opportunity.Discount_Leakage_Percent__c; the dashboard surfaces it alongside the approval workload so pricing policy and audit meet in one view.

  1. Baseline leakage per opportunity from List_Unit_Price__c - Net_Unit_Price__c over list, stored on Discount_Leakage_Percent__c.
  2. Build the leakage report grouped by StageName (Discount_Leakage report in the repo).
  3. Count approvals from Approval_Log__c grouped by Approval_Type__c (Standard vs Executive) to show the queue and the mix.
  4. Compose the dashboard Revenue_Cloud_Dashboard with three tiles — ARR trend, discount leakage, approval workload.
soql
SELECT Discount_Type__c, COUNT(Id) Rows,
       MIN(Lower_Bound__c) MinTier, MAX(Upper_Bound__c) MaxTier
FROM Approval_Log__c
WHERE Decision__c = 'Pending'
GROUP BY Approval_Type__c

SELECT Approval_Type__c, Decision__c, COUNT(Id) Decisions
FROM Approval_Log__c
GROUP BY Approval_Type__c, Decision__c

Expected result A stakeholder reads current ARR, the money lost to discounting per stage, and the approval queue — all from a single screenshot with no further report requests.

Common mistakes

  • Computing leakage from Quote.Discount_Percent__c only and never the opportunity field, mis-stating total loss.
  • Grouping leakage by product instead of by deal/stage, hiding where the money actually bleeds.
  • Including inactive Discount_Schedule__c rows in the baseline, distorting the "leakage" it caused.
  • Omitting the approval workload tile — the dashboard shows the problem but not the queue that approves it.
  • Forgetting the division-by-zero guard when List_Unit_Price__c is 0 or null.

14.2:
Approach Work the five exam-style items below, justify every wrong option, then re-score against the bank.

Blueprint: CPQ — Bundle Configurations / Products / Product Selection; RLM — Catalog Management.

Q1. Which CPQ object represents a selectable option a product exposes when built into a bundle?

  • A. SBQQ__ProductOption__c
  • B. SBQQ__QuoteLine__c
  • C. SBQQ__DiscountTier__c
  • D. SBQQ__PriceCondition__c

Correct: A. SBQQ__ProductOption__c is the container of a configured option inside a bundle. B is a quote line (a quote artifact, not a reusable option), C/D belong to pricing/type of conditional logic. Domain: CPQ — Bundle Configurations.

Q2. A feature with minimum 1 / maximum 1 options forces what?

  • A. exactly one required selection — Correct (the classic pick-one feature)
  • B. a fixed quantity — C. a discount — D. an approval

The min/max contract constrains choices, not quantity, price or workflow. Domain: CPQ — Bundle Configurations.

Q3. Which line field marks the parent row so child lines roll up under it?

  • A. Is_Bundle_Parent__c — Correct
  • B. Bundle_Option__c (names the selected option, not the parent flag)
  • C. List_Unit_Price__c — D. ARR__c

Domain: CPQ — Products / Product Selection.

Q4. An option must be excluded whenever another option is selected. What do you configure?

  • A. a constraint between the two options — Correct
  • B. a price rule — C. a discount schedule — D. a quote template

Mutual exclusion is a configuration constraint; pricing/template objects don't veto selections. Domain: CPQ — Bundle Configurations.

Q5. In RLM, the reusable catalog of sellable products lives on which object?

  • A. ProductCatalog — Correct
  • B. SBQQ__Product__c (legacy namespace)
  • C. Revenue_Sync__e (an event, not a catalog) — D. Discount_Schedule__c (a pricing object)

Domain: RLM — Catalog Management.

soql
SELECT Question_Text__c, Exam_Domain__c, Blueprint_Weight__c, Difficulty__c
FROM Training_Question__c
WHERE Is_Active__c = true
  AND Exam_Domain__c IN ('Bundle Configurations', 'Catalog Management')
ORDER BY Difficulty__c

Expected result Scoring 4/5 or better first pass, with a one-sentence explanation for every wrong option.

Common mistakes

  • Confusing ProductOption (configuration) with QuoteLine (quote detail).
  • Mapping the RLM catalog to SBQQ__Product__c because "it's still a product".
  • Picking a price rule for a mutual-exclusion question; constraints, not pricing, enforce option legality.
  • Treating Is_Bundle_Parent__c and Bundle_Option__c as interchangeable — one flags the parent, the other names the choice.

  • B. Revenue_Schedule__c — C. Training_Question__c — D. Renewal_Opportunity__c

  • B. parallel approval by everyone at once — C. auto-approval after 24 hours — D. a single-step process

  • A. 105000 — Correct — B. 100005 — C. 100500 — D. 5000

FROM Quote
WHERE Approval_Status__c = 'Rejected'

Approach Five items on billing schedules, recognition and the event bus.

  3. Ensure every sellable product has at least one active read-only (standard) or custom Price Book, then add PriceBookEntry rows with List Price.
  4. Where the product drives recurring revenue, store the annual value so Total_ARR__c on Quote and ARR__c on Contract/QuoteLineItem can roll up.

  2. Add a Product Feature per choice group, e.g. "Data Region", "Support Level".

Approach Write SOQL that walks the relationship graph: parent–child inner queries from Quote to QuoteLineItem, then formula/derived totals, and filters on the custom fields from the spec (Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Active__c, Discount_Percent__c).

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Query Quotes with Total_ARR__c, Discount_Percent__c, Approval_Status__c.
  2. Add a child subquery on QuoteLineItems selecting List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, Discount_Percent__c, ARR__c, Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Bundle_Option__c.
  3. Add a second child subquery for Approval_Log__c to surface decisions.
  4. Filter to active, not-fully-discounted lines for a pricing review.
  5. Run the same pattern over Discount_Schedule__c filtered by Discount_Type__c and Active__c.

  (SELECT List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, Discount_Percent__c,

Approach Call BundleConfigurationService.validateConfiguration(quoteId) — the academy service that replays the configured feature/option selections against the product rule engine and returns per-rule results. Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Gather the bundle QuoteLineItems: parent with Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true plus children flagged by Bundle_Option__c.
  2. Invoke the service with the quote Id and read the BundleValidationResult list.
  3. Fail fast: any result with isValid = false blocks the quote from approval.
  4. Map each error back to a human message for the configurator UI.

5.2:
Approach Use PriceRuleEngineService to apply the volume table to quote lines: measure quantity or ARR, resolve the matching Discount_Schedule__c tier, then write the effective discount onto QuoteLineItem.Discount_Percent__c and compute Net_Unit_Price__c from List_Unit_Price__c.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Read the driver from the QuoteLineItem (quantity, or ARR__c × term).
  2. Select the active tier for that Product_Family__c with the driver within Lower_Bound__c/Upper_Bound__c.
  3. Cap the applied discount at a defined ceiling so a tier can never exceed policy.
  4. Recompute Net_Unit_Price__c = List_Unit_Price__c * (1 - Discount_Percent__c/100).
  5. Re-run through QuoteCalculatorService.priceQuote and surface the discount on the quote.

line.Discount_Percent__c = pct;
line.Net_Unit_Price__c   = line.List_Unit_Price__c * (1 - pct / 100);

7.1:
Approach Discount routing decides who must sign when Quote.Discount_Percent__c crosses a band, then persists the decision so the workflow is auditable. ApprovalRoutingService owns the routing decision and Approval_Log__c owns the audit, so the handler stays thin.

  1. Load the quote with the fields that drive routing: Discount_Percent__c and Total_ARR__c.
  2. Call ApprovalRoutingService.determineApprover(discount, totalArr); below the threshold it returns no approver, above it returns the approver from the matching matrix band.
  3. Compare the returned approver against the band the discount falls into (e.g. 0-10, 10-15, 15-20, above 20 where the CFO signs).
  4. Persist the outcome with ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(...), writing Quote__c, Approval_Type__c, Approver__c, Decision__c, Discount_Percent__c, Comments__c and Decision_Date__c.
  5. Mirror the decision onto Quote.Approval_Status__c (Pending Review / Approved / Rejected) so downstream contract generation is gated.
apex
public class DiscountApprovalHandler {
    public static void evaluate(Quote quote) {
        String approver = ApprovalRoutingService.determineApprover(
            quote.Discount_Percent__c,
            quote.Total_ARR__c
        );
        ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(
            quote.Id,
            'Discount',
            approver,
            'Approved',
            quote.Discount_Percent__c,
            'Routed against the discount matrix'
        );
        quote.Approval_Status__c = 'Pending Review';
    }
}

Expected result Running the handler on quotes at 8%, 12%, 18% and 22% discount produces exactly four Approval_Log__c rows — one per quote — each landing on the approver of its band, and every row has a non-null Decision_Date__c. Below threshold (requiresApproval returns false) no approver is assigned.

Common mistakes

  • Routing from a hard-coded percentage instead of quote.Discount_Percent__c, so the audit lies about what was approved.
  • Using >= at the boundary: 25.00% must not auto-route while 25.01% must — inclusive-safe comparison needed.
  • Forgetting to persist: a routed discount with no Approval_Log__c row has no audit trail.
  • Leaving Decision_Date__c null; the exercise verify checks it explicitly.
  • Setting Approval_Status__c but skipping the log, or logging before the approver is resolved.
7.2:
Approach A chain is a strictly ordered sequence of approvers. Each step must be logged before the next step may begin, and the final approver must never be skipped. The chain starts with the threshold approver resolved by ApprovalRoutingService, then appends the deterministic senior steps.

  1. Define the ordered chain — e.g. threshold approver (from determineApprover), then Sales Director, then VP of Sales.
  2. Resolve the first step via ApprovalRoutingService.determineApprover(quote.Discount_Percent__c, quote.Total_ARR__c).
  3. Iterate the chain in index order and call logDecision once per step, stamping Decision__c = 'Pending' and a step label in Comments__c.
  4. Escalate: if an earlier approver is skipped (recalled or out-of-scope), append the final approver and log it last — never drop it.
  5. Verify no step can start before its predecessor's Approval_Log__c row exists (ordering is enforced by the loop, not faith).
apex
List<String> chain = new List<String>{
    ApprovalRoutingService.determineApprover(
        quote.Discount_Percent__c,
        quote.Total_ARR__c
    ),
    'Sales Director',
    'VP of Sales'
};

for (Integer i = 0; i < chain.size(); i++) {
    ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(
        quote.Id,
        'Discount',
        chain[i],
        'Pending',
        quote.Discount_Percent__c,
        'Step ' + (i + 1) + ' of chain'
    );
}

Expected result SELECT Id, Approver__c, Decision__c, Decision_Date__c FROM Approval_Log__c WHERE Quote__c = :id ORDER BY Decision_Date__c returns the steps in chain order — first the threshold approver, then Sales Director, then VP of Sales — with no gap and the final approver present in every run.

Common mistakes

  • Inserting rows together without an explicit order, so the "chain" has no sequence.
  • Skipping the recursion guard: the update in a trigger context can re-fire and duplicate chain rows (QuoteTriggerHandlerService.shouldRun).
  • Logging the chain after the fact instead of before inviting the next approver.
  • Letting the final approver disappear when an early step is skipped.
  • Using Decision__c values that the log can't represent (Approval_Log__c expects Pending/Approved/Rejected/Recalled).
8.1:
Approach Contracting materializes an accepted quote into a Draft contract. The quote is the source of truth: term and pricing fields must be copied verbatim so the contract, the quote and downstream renewal logic never diverge.

  1. Accept the quote and read its term values (Contract_Term_Months__c, Total_ARR__c, Is_Renewal__c, Uplift_Percent__c).
  2. Create the Contract with AccountId from the quote.
  3. Copy ARR__c = quote.Total_ARR__c and Renewal_Term_Months__c = quote.Contract_Term_Months__c; carry Uplift_Percent__c.
  4. Set Auto_Renew__c from the quote flag and CPQ_Contract_Status__c = 'Draft' (standard Status = 'Draft').
  5. Insert the contract, then generate the contract document via ContractGenerationService.

Contract contract = new Contract(
    AccountId = quote.AccountId,
    ARR__c = quote.Total_ARR__c,

    Renewal_Term_Months__c = quote.Contract_Term_Months__c,
    Uplift_Percent__c = quote.Uplift_Percent__c,

  • Forgetting AccountId: the contract insert throws a required-field exception.
  • Copying List_Unit_Price__c from a line instead of Total_ARR__c from the quote — wrong magnitude.
  • Hard-coding Renewal_Term_Months__c instead of inheriting the quote term.
  • Generating the document against a quote that is still Not Submitted — gate on Approval_Status__c = 'Approved'.
  • Letting a re-calc after acceptance change the quote while the contract keeps the old ARR; contract and quote must stay equal.

    RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline(contract.Id)[0];

    renewal.ARR__c,
    renewal.Uplift_Percent__c
);

renewal.ARR__c = upliftedArr;
renewal.Status__c = 'In Progress';
update renewal;

Expected result A 1000 ARR contract with 10% uplift produces Renewal_Opportunity__c.ARR__c = 1100, the row links Account__c and Contract__c, and Renewal_Date__c/Status__c are populated. The whole window produces exactly one opportunity per in-scope contract.

Common mistakes

  • Applying uplift twice — buildRenewalPipeline already computes calculateUpliftedARR internally, so re-applying inflates the number.
  • Miscomputing the uplift: arr * (100 + pct) / 100, not arr + pct.
  • Leaving Uplift_Percent__c null, which calculateUpliftedARR treats as 0 and silently drops the increase.
  • Creating opportunities for contracts already renewed (no re-entry guard → duplicates when the batch re-runs).
  • Forgetting to set Status__c, so the pipeline shows empty/stale rows in the ARR report.
9.1:
Approach After the contract exists, the order becomes the record fulfillment and billing act on. The order is derived from the contracted quote so its lines, ARR and status are the executed truth.

  2. Build the order with one line per QuoteLineItem via OrderFulfillmentService.ordersFromContract(contract.Id).
  3. Copy Total_ARR__c = contract.ARR__c so the order inherits the executed contract value, not a stale quote total.
  4. Seed Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Pending', clear Fulfillment_Date__c and leave ERP_Order_Number__c blank.
  5. Activate the order so it becomes eligible for fulfillment processing.

9.2:
Approach Fulfillment is a state machine over Fulfillment_Status__c: Pending → In Progress → Shipped → Fulfilled, with Integration Failed reachable when the ERP never confirms. Validation and date stamping live in the service so flows and integrations cannot skip steps or drive an order backwards.

  1. Call updateFulfillmentStatus(orderId, 'In Progress', Date.today()) to move the order off Pending.
  2. Call advanceFulfillment(orderId) twice to walk Shipped then Fulfilled.
  3. When the ERP confirms, write its reference into ERP_Order_Number__c.
  4. Confirm Fulfillment_Date__c is stamped only when the order reaches completion.

    Date.today()

OrderFulfillmentService.advanceFulfillment(orderId);
OrderFulfillmentService.advanceFulfillment(orderId);

Expected result The order ends at Fulfilled with ERP_Order_Number__c and Fulfillment_Date__c populated. Any attempt to move from Pending straight to Fulfilled, or to revert an advanced status, is rejected — the flow keeps dates accurate.

Common mistakes

  • Jumping statuses instead of advancing one valid step at a time, skipping the audit of intermediate states.
  • Allowing backward transitions (Fulfilled back to Shipped) because no transition validation exists.
  • Stamping Fulfillment_Date__c at Pending — the date must reflect actual delivery, not order creation.
  • Ignoring the ERP payload, leaving ERP_Order_Number__c null and breaking the external reconciliation.
  • Letting an unconfirmed order ride in Integration Failed forever without a retry path that increments status and re-advances.
CAP:
Solution overview The capstone orchestrates every service in one quote-to-cash flow: catalog and pricing, configuration, quoting, approval, contracting, renewal projection, order fulfillment, billing, revenue recognition, integration and analytics. It proves the academy model end to end — a rep configures a bundle on an approved, discounted quote; the win generates a contract, order and billing/recognition schedules; the ERP syncs through the event bus; and dashboards report the deal as ARR, leakage and recognized revenue.

P1:
Solution overview An end-to-end CPQ data model must carry a deal from an Opportunity through a configured, priced and approved Quote into a Contract, then an Order with billing and recognition, and finally loop back through renewal. The model has four layers: the sell side (Opportunity → Quote → QuoteLineItem → PriceBookEntry → Product2), the pricing and control layer (Discount_Schedule__c, Approval_Log__c), the cash side (Contract → Order → Revenue_Schedule__c), and the renewal loop (Renewal_Opportunity__c). The same deal must translate to the RLM engine built on core objects (ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel, PriceBookEntry) so one model serves both engines.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Opportunity layer — hang the deal on Opportunity with ARR__c, CPQ_Quote_Status__c, Discount_Leakage_Percent__c, Renewal_Date__c and Is_Strategic__c so dashboards can measure pipeline value and leakage.
  2. Quote layer — link Opportunity → Quote via OpportunityId and store the commerce state: Approval_Status__c, Discount_Percent__c, Contract_Term_Months__c, Is_Renewal__c, CPQ_Sync_Status__c, Total_ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c.
  3. Line layer — QuoteLineItem carries List_Unit_Price__c, Net_Unit_Price__c, Discount_Percent__c, ARR__c and the bundle markers Is_Bundle_Parent__c, Bundle_Option__c; each line joins through PriceBookEntry to Product2 in a Pricebook2.
  4. Control layer — Discount_Schedule__c (Discount_Type__c, Lower_Bound__c, Upper_Bound__c, Discount_Percent__c, Product_Family__c, Active__c) feeds pricing; Approval_Log__c (Quote__c, Approval_Type__c, Approver__c, Decision__c, Discount_Percent__c, Comments__c, Decision_Date__c) records every approval decision.
  5. Cash layer — Contract (with ARR__c, Auto_Renew__c, Renewal_Term_Months__c, Uplift_Percent__c, CPQ_Contract_Status__c) and Order (Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, ERP_Order_Number__c, Total_ARR__c) feed Revenue_Schedule__c via the four lookups Quote__c, Contract__c, Order__c, Account__c.
  6. Renewal loop — Renewal_Opportunity__c (Account__c, Contract__c, Renewal_Date__c, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c, Status__c) closes the loop back into a new Quote.
  7. RLM translation — map legacy-managed-package products to core: Product2 → ProductCatalog, price book membership → ProductSellingModel + PriceBookEntry, subscriptions → billing/recognition schedules.

P10:
Solution overview Legacy CPQ is the managed package (SBQQ__ objects); Revenue Cloud / RLM is the next-generation platform on core objects (ProductCatalog, ProductSellingModel, PriceBookEntry on Product2/Pricebook2). Migration is extract, transform, load, verify and cutover — moving products, price books, configured bundles, assets and subscriptions into the RLM catalog and revenue objects while preserving the IDs and history that downstream integrations depend on. The Revenue_Sync__e bus with Integration_Type__c = 'MigrationSync' provides a replayable ingestion channel so load failures are retried, not re-entered.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Inventory the source — report every SBQQ__ object family: products and options, price books and entries, quotes and lines, contracted subscriptions and their schedules.
  2. Map the schema — build the translation table SBQQ__ field → RLM field (e.g. legacy product option → core ProductOption/feature; price book membership → PriceBook2/PriceBookEntry; sold subscription → revenue contract line + billing schedule).
  3. Extract with SOQL — read the legacy records in batchable chunks; keep the legacy Id in a staging key so the transform can reference parents.
  4. Transform in Apex — map families and flags: bundle parents become core bundle products with features/options; CPQ_Enabled__c accounts gate which products migrate.
  5. Load through the event bus — publish each row as a Revenue_Sync__e with Source_Object__c = 'SBQQ__*', JSON Payload__c, Direction__c = 'Inbound', and Retry_Count__c start 0; the subscriber upserts the RLM object and increments retries on failure.
  6. Verify with row-count checks — compare legacy counts against RLM counts per object; assert price sums match and every migrated quote links to a migrated opportunity.
  7. Cut over — switch the UI/rules to RLM, keep legacy read-only for audit, then archive SBQQ__ records after a freeze window.

  • Migrating products but forgetting their price book entries, so no product is sellable.
  • Copying SBQQ__ fields blindly into fields with different semantics on core objects.

P2:
Solution overview A configurable bundle is a parent line plus option lines. In the academy model the parent QuoteLineItem carries Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true and each option line sets Bundle_Option__c using the convention "Group: Option" (for example "Storage: 100 GB"). The bundle is worth the roll-up of its selected options, single-select groups reject two options from the same group, and the bundle must never reach pricing before its shape is valid.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Seed the catalog — create the bundle Product2 (e.g. "Secure Workspace") and option products, publish each into the standard Pricebook2 via PriceBookEntry.
  2. Insert the parent line — add a QuoteLineItem with Is_Bundle_Parent__c = true and a list/net price.
  3. Insert the option lines — one line per selectable option, each with Bundle_Option__c in Group: Option form and an ARR__c; quantity 1 so the roll-up is not double-counted.
  4. Validate the shape — call BundleConfigurationService.validateBundleConfiguration(lines); it flags a parent with no options and orphan options with no parent.
  5. Check single-select groups — call BundleConfigurationService.hasConflictingOptions(lines), which uses the group prefix of Bundle_Option__c to detect two distinct options in the same group.
  6. Price the bundle — call BundleConfigurationService.rollupBundlePrice(lines); a parent with options is replaced by its option sum, a bare parent keeps its own price.
  7. Refresh quote totals — write the resolved net prices back to the lines and call QuoteCalculatorService.recalculateTotals so Total_ARR__c and Discount_Percent__c reflect the final configuration.

];

  • Option lines use the exact Group: Option naming convention

Common mistakes

  • Pricing before validating, so an invalid configuration quotes a price anyway.
  • Not scoping the bundle query to the parent/option markers and double counting rows.
  • Forgetting Bundle_Option__c must begin with the group so single-select conflict detection works.
  • Letting a bare parent (no options) silently price at zero instead of its fallback price.

P3:
Solution overview Approval is a matrix, not a single rule: the required sign-off depends on discount depth and deal attributes. ApprovalRoutingService provides the core: requiresApproval(discountPercent) (true only when the discount is strictly above the 25% threshold), determineApprover(percent) (finds an active user whose Profile or Role matches %Approver%), and logDecision(quoteId, decision, discountPercent, comments), which persists an Approval_Log__c row stamped Approval_Type__c = 'Discount (Executive)' above 25% or 'Discount (Standard)' at or below it. The matrix layers region, partner tier and strategic flags on top of these two service levels to decide whether a deal is escalated at all — never overriding the types the service stamps.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Define the bands — a deal whose effective discount stays at or below 25% is Discount (Standard) and needs no sign-off; anything strictly above 25% is Discount (Executive) and must be escalated. The 25% constant is the service's APPROVAL_THRESHOLD_PCT.
  2. Load the deal attributes — read the Quote's Total_ARR__c, the Account's Region__c and Partner_Tier__c, and the Opportunity's Is_Strategic__c; strategic or big-ARR deals apply a surcharge so borderline discounts also escalate.
  3. Route with the service — compute the effective percentage (base + strategic/region surcharge), then use requiresApproval to decide whether sign-off is needed at all and determineApprover to pick the approver user.
  4. Log the decision — logDecision writes Approval_Log__c with the service-stamped type, the approver, Discount_Percent__c, Decision__c and Decision_Date__c; passing the raw (surrounding) percentage keeps the audit trail faithful to the deal.
  5. Persist the matrix — store the surcharge and any family-specific thresholds in Discount_Schedule__c rows (Discount_Type__c = 'Approval', bounds in discount points) so finance can tune the matrix without code changes.
  6. Wire the trigger — on Quote update, re-evaluate any quote whose Discount_Percent__c moved; QuoteTriggerHandlerService.beforeUpdate preserves the prior Approval_Status__c while the routing runs.
  7. Notify — send the Quote_Discount_Approval email template to the approver with the decision link.

Decimal surcharge = matrixByRegion.get(account.Region__c); // worked example: 5 pts
Decimal effective = (dealDiscount != null ? dealDiscount : 0) + (surcharge != null ? surcharge : 0);
String band = ApprovalRoutingService.requiresApproval(effective)
    ? 'Discount (Executive)'
    : 'Discount (Standard)';

if (ApprovalRoutingService.requiresApproval(effective)) {
    Approval_Log__c log = ApprovalRoutingService.logDecision(
        quote.Id, 'Pending', dealDiscount,
        'Matrix band = ' + band + ', strategic = ' + opportunity.Is_Strategic__c);
    System.debug('Escalated to ' + band + ' | approver = ' + log.Approver__c);
} else {
    System.debug('Falls within ' + band + ' band - no signature required.');
}

  • Approval matrix documented as bands × region × strategic escalation
  • Directives are routed through ApprovalRoutingService
  • Approver resolution verified (determineApprover returns a real user or a manual fallback)
  • Approval_Log__c rows carry the correct type, approver, decision and date
  • Threshold edits served from Discount_Schedule__c rather than hard-coded values

Expected result A 22% non-strategic quote passes without sign-off; a 26% quote is stamped Discount (Executive) with an approver resolved by determineApprover; a 23% regional deal with a 5-point matrix surcharge escalates because the effective 28% crosses the threshold; every decision lands on Approval_Log__c with a matching Decision_Date__c, and Approval_Status__c on the Quote transitions only when the log records a decision.

Common mistakes

  • Treating exactly 25.00% as approvable — the service is strict > 25.
  • Escalating purely on discount % and ignoring strategic/region attributes.
  • Logging a decision before checking requiresApproval, creating noisy feed.
  • Hard-coding approvers instead of resolving via the service query.
  • Letting the approval trigger re-fire forever without shouldRun/clear recursion guards.

Solution overview An automated quote document renders the live, priced, approved Quote into a signed deliverable without a rep re-typing numbers. A document template binds Quote and QuoteLineItem merge fields, sections mirror the way a customer reads a proposal (header, line items, totals, terms, signature), and generation fires automatically once the quote leaves a DRAFT approval state. Because the numbers come from the same fields QuoteCalculatorService writes, the printed document always matches the record.

P5:
Solution overview Contract automation has two halves. First, a won (or accepted) quote is materialized into a Draft Contract by ContractGenerationService — generateContract(Quote) for singles and generateContracts(List<Quote>) for trigger batches, sharing one buildFromQuote that carries term, ARR, auto-renew and uplift. Second, contracts about to expire or auto-renew are projected into Renewal_Opportunity__c rows by RenewalQuoteService, which computes uplifted ARR and sets the renewal date from the contract term.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Accept the quote — move the quote past approval; in the flow this drives contract creation so no rep action is needed.
  2. Create the contract — call generateContract for a single winner or generateContracts in the trigger for the whole batch (one DML statement).
  3. Populate renewal drivers — set Auto_Renew__c from Quote.Is_Renewal__c, Uplift_Percent__c from the quote, ARR__c from Total_ARR__c, and CPQ_Contract_Status__c to a tracking status.
  4. Activate and schedule — activate the contract so standard EndDate and renewal timing are computed from StartDate + ContractTerm.
  5. Build the renewal pipeline — in ContractTrigger call RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline(contracts); each contract becomes a Renewal_Opportunity__c with Status__c = 'Open' and Renewal_Date__c at the end of its term.
  6. Uplift the value — calculateUpliftedARR(arr, upliftPercent) computes arr * (1 + uplift/100), e.g. 120,000 ARR at 5% → 126,000.
  7. Remind — the Renewal_Reminder email template notifies the owning rep as Renewal_Date__c approaches.
apex
// Materialize three won quotes in one trigger batch (single DML).
List<Contract> contracts = ContractGenerationService.generateContracts(wonQuotes);
System.debug('Created ' + contracts.size() + ' draft contracts');

// Renewal window projection: auto-renewing and expiring contracts.
List<Renewal_Opportunity__c> pipeline =
    RenewalQuoteService.buildRenewalPipeline(expiringContracts);
for (Renewal_Opportunity__c opp : pipeline) {
    System.debug('Renewal for ' + opp.Account__c +
        ' | date=' + opp.Renewal_Date__c +
        ' | ARR=' + opp.ARR__c + ' at uplift ' + opp.Uplift_Percent__c);
}

Deliverables checklist

  • Won-quote → Draft Contract flow wired (single + bulk paths)
  • Renewal drivers (Auto_Renew__c, Renewal_Term_Months__c, Uplift_Percent__c) set from the quote
  • ContractTrigger builds the renewal pipeline with one DML statement
  • calculateUpliftedARR verified against a hand-computed example
  • Renewal reminders scheduled via the email template

Expected result Accepting quote Q (12 months, 120,000 ARR, Uplift 5) creates a Draft 12-month contract with matching ARR; activating it projects a Renewal_Opportunity__c dated at the contract end with ARR 126,000 and Status Open. Because buildRenewalPipeline inserts without a dedupe guard, the trigger must fire once per contract lifecycle (for example only on activation) so the pipeline never double-counts a contract.

Common mistakes

  • Inserting contracts inside a loop and hitting the 150-DML governor.
  • Activating a contract with no EndDate so the renewal date defaults to today.
  • Forgetting to carry Uplift_Percent__c, so renewals understate future ARR.
  • Creating a renewal opportunity from an already-amended contract and double counting.
  • Building the pipeline synchronously per contract instead of one batched insert.
P6:
Solution overview A subscription must bill predictably. BillingScheduleService turns annual value into monthly rows on Revenue_Schedule__c using straight-line splitting with the remainder forced onto the LAST period, so the rows always re-sum exactly to the ARR. buildBillingSchedule(Quote, termMonths) builds rows in memory (no DML); createRevenueSchedules(List<Order>) builds and inserts, cascading term/ARR from each order's Quote and skipping orders already scheduled so the trigger can re-fire safely.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Retrieve a priced quote — need Total_ARR__c > 0 and an Account; a null or negative ARR returns an empty schedule.
  2. Build the schedule — call buildBillingSchedule(q, term); each period row gets Recognition_Method__c = 'Straight Line', Status__c = 'Pending', Period__c = 'M1'..'M'+term, Recognition_Date__c = today + i months and Source_Type__c = 'Billing'.
  3. Persist or defer — either insert the builder's rows at contract signing or let createRevenueSchedules do it when the Order is created.
  4. Cascade from the Order — createRevenueSchedules reads Quote.Contract_Term_Months__c and Quote.Total_ARR__c, falling back to 12 months and the Order's Total_ARR__c.
  5. Guarantee idempotency — the service queries existing Revenue_Schedule__c.Order__c values first and skips orders already scheduled, so every fulfillment-status update does not fabricate a second schedule.
  6. Verify the sum — assert SUM(Amount__c) == Total_ARR__c; uneven values put the rounding delta on the last row.
apex
Quote q = [SELECT Id, AccountId, Total_ARR__c, Contract_Term_Months__c
           FROM Quote WHERE Id = :quoteId LIMIT 1];
Integer term = q.Contract_Term_Months__c != null ? Integer.valueOf(q.Contract_Term_Months__c) : 12;

List<Revenue_Schedule__c> sched = BillingScheduleService.buildBillingSchedule(q, term);
insert sched; // publisher or order flow decides the moment of persistence

Decimal total = 0;
for (Revenue_Schedule__c r : sched) {
    total += r.Amount__c;
    System.debug(r.Period__c + ' ' + r.Recognition_Date__c + ' ' + r.Amount__c);
}
System.assert(total == q.Total_ARR__c, 'Schedule must re-sum to ARR exactly.');

Deliverables checklist

  • Billing schedule built for a 12,000 ARR × 12-month quote
  • Rows use Recognition_Method__c = Straight Line, Status = Pending, Period M1..M12
  • Remainder lands on the final period (sum equals ARR exactly)
  • createRevenueSchedules invoked from OrderTrigger proves idempotency
  • Term/ARR cascade verified from quote, with fallback to 12 months

Expected result A 12,000 ARR quote with a 12-month term produces 12 rows of 1,000 each dated one month apart and source 'Billing'; after order creation the same 12 rows reappear with Order__c populated and source 'Order', and a second Order update does not duplicate them. A 12,005 ARR quote yields eleven rows of 1,000.42 and a final remainder row so the total still equals 12,005.

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by term and never reconciling rounding, so rows sum to less than ARR.
  • Inserting inside the trigger loop (DML governor) instead of one batched insert.
  • Re-running the schedule on every Order update because idempotency was skipped.
  • Using quote ARR but the order's 12-month default, producing a mismatched schedule.
  • Forgetting to set Recognition_Date__c, so recognition automation later skips the rows.
P7:
Solution overview Recognition is the accounting side of the same billing rows. Under ASC 606 / IFRS 15, revenue is recognized as performance obligations are satisfied; here the straight-line billing schedule becomes a recognition schedule. RevenueRecognitionService provides three pieces: recognizeRevenue(Set<Id>) marks due rows Recognized and writes Recognized_Amount__c; calculateRecognizedAmount(row, asOf) is the deterministic per-row math; and rollupAccountARR(Set<Id>) re-aggregates recognized amounts onto Account.Current_ARR__c with a reset-then-sum so stale values never survive.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Run a daily job — a scheduled Apex or RevenueScheduleTrigger gathers Revenue_Schedule__c rows whose Recognition_Date__c <= today and whose Status__c != 'Recognized'.
  2. Recognize due rows — recognizeRevenue(scheduleIds) selects candidates in one query, computes each Recognized_Amount__c via calculateRecognizedAmount, flips Status__c to 'Recognized' and updates in one DML.
  3. Keep the math testable — calculateRecognizedAmount(row, asOf) returns the existing recognized amount for a Recognized row, the full Amount__c when Recognition_Date__c <= asOf, and 0 otherwise; assert it across date cases.
  4. Roll up to the account — rollupAccountARR(accountIds) zeroes every in-scope account, re-sums Recognized_Amount__c with GROUP BY, and writes Current_ARR__c in exactly two DML statements.
  5. Prevent double recognition — never re-recognize a row that is already 'Recognized'; the query filter plus the guard in step 1 is the protection.
  6. Report — recognize-month views use Recognition_Method__c, Recognition_Date__c and the status to reconcile actuals vs forecast.
apex
// Daily batch driver
Set<Id> scheduleIds = new Set<Id>();
for (Revenue_Schedule__c s : [
    SELECT Id FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
    WHERE Recognition_Date__c <= TODAY AND Status__c != 'Recognized'
]) { scheduleIds.add(s.Id); }

RevenueRecognitionService.recognizeRevenue(scheduleIds);

Set<Id> accountIds = new Set<Id>();
for (Revenue_Schedule__c r : [
    SELECT Account__c FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
    WHERE Account__c != null AND Recognition_Date__c <= TODAY
]) { accountIds.add(r.Account__c); }
if (!accountIds.isEmpty()) {
    RevenueRecognitionService.rollupAccountARR(accountIds);
}

Deliverables checklist

  • Daily recognition job selects only due, non-recognized rows
  • calculateRecognizedAmount unit-tested for recognized, due and future rows
  • rollupAccountARR verified to reset-then-sum without loops
  • Re-running the job recognizes nothing twice
  • Account.Current_ARR__c matches the sum of recognized rows

Expected result After the job runs, every row dated on or before today has Status__c = 'Recognized' and Recognized_Amount__c = Amount__c; future rows stay 'Pending'; the account's Current_ARR__c equals the sum of recognized amounts (120,000 after a full 12-month, 120,000 ARR contract is recognized). Deleting all schedules for an account zeroes its Current ARR instead of leaving stale value.

Common mistakes

  • Recognizing rows before their Recognition_Date__c, distorting the month of record.
  • Summing Amount__c instead of Recognized_Amount__c so partially recognized deals over-report.
  • Re-recognizing the same rows on every trigger fire — the status filter is the guard.
  • Updating each schedule in a loop and blowing the DML governor.
  • Forgetting the reset-then-sum pattern, leaving stale Current_ARR__c on accounts whose schedules were deleted.
P8:
Solution overview Quote-to-cash integration decouples Salesforce from back-office systems with a replayable event contract. Revenue_Sync__e is the platform-event bus: producers publish a change, subscribers react, and a failure can be retried without losing the message. QuoteTriggerHandlerService.afterUpdate publishes an event every time Approval_Status__c changes, populated with Source_Object__c = 'Quote', a JSON Payload__c, Direction__c, Status__c, a random Correlation_Id__c, Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync' and Endpoint__c such as 'RevenueCloudEventBus'. Downstream, the ERP confirms the order with ERP_Order_Number__c and fulfillment progress flows back.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. Define the event contract — agree on Payload__c JSON fields (quoteId, approvalStatus, totalArr, discountPercent) once; producers and consumers share the schema.
  2. Publish on change — afterUpdate compares old vs new Approval_Status__c inside a shouldRun/clear recursion guard so one transition publishes exactly one event batch.
  3. Subscribe — RevenueSyncEventTrigger handles Revenue_Sync__e after insert; a Flow or Apex handler routes the payload (e.g. to the ERP, or logging for this project).
  4. Write back the result — the ERP response flips Quote.CPQ_Sync_Status__c to 'Synced' and the Order gets its ERP_Order_Number__c; Direction__c marks the return trip.
  5. Handle failure — on subscriber error, mark Status__c = 'Failed', bump Retry_Count__c, and schedule a retry consume of the same correlation id.
  6. Trace end to end — every step logs with Correlation_Id__c so a single deal can be traced from quote → event → ERP order → fulfillment.
apex
// Fragment of QuoteTriggerHandlerService.afterUpdate pattern
List<Revenue_Sync__e> events = new List<Revenue_Sync__e>();
for (Quote q : newQuotes) {
    Quote old = oldMap.get(q.Id);
    if (old != null && old.Approval_Status__c != q.Approval_Status__c) {
        events.add(new Revenue_Sync__e(
            Source_Object__c = 'Quote',
            Payload__c = JSON.serialize(new Map<String, Object>{
                'quoteId' => q.Id, 'approvalStatus' => q.Approval_Status__c,
                'totalArr' => q.Total_ARR__c, 'discountPercent' => q.Discount_Percent__c
            }),
            Direction__c = 'Outbound', Status__c = q.Approval_Status__c,
            Correlation_Id__c = String.valueOf(Crypto.getRandomLong()),
            Integration_Type__c = 'ApprovalSync', Endpoint__c = 'RevenueCloudEventBus'));
    }
}
if (!events.isEmpty()) { EventBus.publish(events); }

Deliverables checklist

  • Event schema documented for Payloadc, Directionc, Integration_Type__c
  • Approval transitions publish exactly one event batch (recursion guard)
  • Subscriber logs and dispatches the payload correctly
  • ERP write-back sets CPQ_Sync_Status__c and ERP_Order_Number__c
  • Retry path bumps Retry_Count__c and re-consumes the correlation id

Expected result Changing a quote from 'Not Submitted' to 'In Approval' emits one Revenue_Sync__e event with the quote id, approval state, ARR and discount in the payload; the subscriber logs it; the ERP response marks CPQ_Sync_Status__c = 'Synced' and the newly created Order carries ERP_Order_Number__c. Re-transmitting the approval change does not republish because the guard only lets the first invocation through.

Common mistakes

  • Publishing inside the DML loop or without the recursion guard, flooding the bus.
  • Changing the payload schema mid-flight with no versioning, breaking consumers.
  • Swallowing subscriber errors so retries never happen and deals silently desync.
  • Overwriting ERP_Order_Number__c on every sync instead of treating it as write-once.
  • Logging by quote only and losing the correlation trail across systems.
P9:
Solution overview The dashboard answers four executive questions: how much is in the pipeline (ARR), how much is leaking (discounts), how much has been billed vs recognized (revenue quality), and what renewals are coming (retention). It reads only the academy model — Opportunity, Quote, QuoteLineItem, Approval_Log__c, Contract, Order, Revenue_Schedule__c, Renewal_Opportunity__c and Account — and uses SOQL aggregates plus report types, not guesswork.

Numbered implementation steps:

  1. ARR pipeline — report on Opportunity (ARR__c, CPQ_Quote_Status__c) and Quote (Total_ARR__c) filtered by status; a funnel shows draft → submitted → approved → won.
  2. Discount leakage — plot Opportunity.Discount_Leakage_Percent__c by Region and by Quote.Discount_Percent__c; flag quotes whose approval type was 'Discount (Executive)' from Approval_Log__c.
  3. Billing vs recognition — on Revenue_Schedule__c, sum Amount__c by Status__c and month; recognized quality = Recognized_Amount__c / Amount__c per period.
  4. Renewal book — list Renewal_Opportunity__c by Renewal_Date__c, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c and Status__c; overlay with the Renewal_Reminder schedule.
  5. Account health — Account.Current_ARR__c and Renewal_Risk__c on a scorecard, drilled by Region__c and Partner_Tier__c.
  6. Certification analytics — Training_Question__c by Exam_Domain__c and Blueprint_Weight__c to show study readiness alongside the revenue KPIs.
  7. Define report types — build cross-object report types (Quote with Approval_Log__c, Contract with Renewal_Opportunity__c, Order with Revenue_Schedule__c) so every dashboard chart joins at the record level rather than screen-scraping.
  8. Add formula metrics — compute net bookings per line as Quantity * Net_Unit_Price__c and leakage per quote as 100 - (Net_Total / List_Total * 100) with the same math QuoteCalculatorService.calculateDiscountPercent uses, keeping the dashboard and the calculator in agreement.
  9. Refresh & alert — schedule the dashboard subscription weekly, and raise a custom alert list of quotes whose Discount_Percent__c exceeds 25 so reps see approval risk before close.
soql
SELECT Quote__c, SUM(Amount__c) Billed, SUM(Recognized_Amount__c) Recognized,
       Status__c, Recognition_Method__c
FROM Revenue_Schedule__c
WHERE Recognition_Date__c = THIS_YEAR
GROUP BY Quote__c, Status__c, Recognition_Method__c

SELECT Account__c, Renewal_Date__c, ARR__c, Uplift_Percent__c, Status__c
FROM Renewal_Opportunity__c
WHERE Renewal_Date__c < NEXT_MONTH AND Status__c = 'Open'
ORDER BY Renewal_Date__c

SELECT Account.Region__c, SUM(ARR__c) PipelineARR, AVG(Discount_Leakage_Percent__c) AvgLeakage
FROM Opportunity
WHERE IsClosed = false
GROUP BY Account.Region__c
ORDER BY PipelineARR DESC

Deliverables checklist

  • ARR pipeline funnel report (quote stage × Total_ARR__c)
  • Discount leakage report by region and approval type
  • Billing vs recognized report on Revenue_Schedule__c aggregates
  • Renewal pipeline report on Renewal_Opportunity__c
  • Dashboard composed with Account health + training readiness widgets

Expected result The dashboard shows e.g. 480,000 pipeline ARR in the funnel, an average leakage rising with discount band, 45,000 billed of which 30,000 recognized, and 126,000 of renewals landing next quarter at 5% uplift. Every number traces back to a service-generated row, so finance and sales agree on the same source of truth.

Common mistakes

  • Mixing billing and recognition rows in one total so recognized revenue is overstated.
  • Reporting leakage only at the quote level and hiding opportunity-level dilution.
  • Comparing pipeline ARR from Opportunity against Total_ARR__c from Quote without a stage filter.
  • Building the dashboard on report snapshots that never refresh recognition data.
  • Ignoring Active__c/status filters so draft quotes inflate the funnel.
